speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for presenting. You mentioned a chest skin lesion; can you tell me how long it has been present and if it has changed in size or color?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the growth over two months is concerning. Given your history of diabetes and hypercholesterolemia, have you noticed any changes in your overall skin, such as new bumps or warts elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

Based on your age, the 2-month history of a painless but enlarging chest lesion, and your significant history of diabetes and hypercholesterolemia (risk factors for skin issues and poor wound healing), this clinical picture is highly suspicious for a non-melanoma skin cancer. While basal cell carcinoma is also possible, the rapid growth and specific location warrant immediate histological confirmation. Do you have any personal or family history of skin cancer?
